text: Refining D-0216 and D-0217 after #355's second review: a method named on its class resolves only when its code was compiled in that class's own body under that name, and counts only when called on that class, an instance or a subclass, by the receiver's real type, which no __class__ property changes; a C method must belong to the class named, and a module function whose code is a closure's, or a builtin that import or class statements reach, as __import__, is refused. An application declaration's code counts only with its staged module's globals, and any other only with the globals it was defined with, so a copy compiled again from the staged source counts nothing. A throw into a generator, as close() makes, counts no call. Only assertions the test method makes, directly or through code it calls, count, never setUp's, tearDown's or a cleanup's, and only the callable forms of assertRaises and assertWarns and their Regex variants hand what they call, with any generator handed it to resume, and only while they run. Nothing ties a passing assertion to the call it checks, so the assertion requirement keeps out a test that asserts nothing, not one that asserts the wrong thing. In-process tampering with the runner is out of scope for backing tests, as D-0183 says it is for drivers.
